zipCodeComparison.areaName: Southern & Western Clifton (Suburban & Higher Assessed Values)
zipCodeComparison.neighborhoodsIncluded: Montclair Heights, Allwood, Richfield, Athenia, Albion, Styertowne, Maple Valley, Yanticaw
keyFindings: Generates ~63% of Clifton's residential property tax levy due to higher assessed single-family properties.
Significantly older median age (45.4 yrs) with a high concentration of empty-nesters and senior citizens.
Fewer public school students per 100 households compared to 07011, meaning 07013 heavily subsidizes the district budget.
High homeownership rate (73.6%) means residents pay tax bills directly via escrow or quarterly checks.

zipCodeComparison.neighborhoodsIncluded: Botany Village, Lakeview, Main Avenue Corridor, Dutch Hill
keyFindings: Higher tax-to-income economic burden (13.55% vs 12.24%) despite lower gross assessed values.
Significantly younger median age (37.2 yrs) with high birth rates and school enrollment (supplies 53.2% of public school students).
Majority-renter population (52.2%) where tenants pay property taxes indirectly embedded in monthly apartment rent ($300-$450/month of rent).
High concentration of multi-family (2-to-4 family) properties and immigrant-owned commercial small businesses.

neighborhoods.name: Montclair Heights
neighborhoods.description: Hilly wooded neighborhood bordering Montclair and Upper Montclair. Characterized by large single-family colonial homes, expansive yards, and low housing turnover.
neighborhoods.taxDynamic: Pays the highest average property tax check in Clifton (~$18k/year). Demographics skew older with established professionals and many retirees.

neighborhoods.name: Allwood & Richfield
neighborhoods.description: Historic suburban neighborhoods centered around Allwood Road, Styertowne Shopping Center, and Route 3. Stable middle-to-upper-middle-class enclave.
neighborhoods.taxDynamic: High proportion of long-time senior homeowners on fixed incomes who feel intense pressure when annual school budgets and county tax levies rise.

neighborhoods.name: Athenia
neighborhoods.description: Centrally located around Clifton Avenue and Athenia Steel Park. Walkable neighborhood with a balance of single-family homes, duplexes, and local bakeries.
neighborhoods.taxDynamic: Represents Clifton's statistical midpoint. Even balance of school-age families and senior residents paying ~$12,000 annually in taxes.

neighborhoods.name: Delawanna & Transit Corridor
neighborhoods.description: Located at Clifton's southern border near Nutley, Passaic River, and Route 3. Features the Delawanna NJ Transit train station, townhouse complexes, and heavy commercial retail.
neighborhoods.taxDynamic: Higher proportion of transit commuters and young working professionals. Heavy commercial ratables help offset residential municipal costs.

neighborhoods.name: Botany Village & Historic District
neighborhoods.character: Historic Industrial Textile Mill & High Density
neighborhoods.description: Historic neighborhood built around the former Botany Worsted Mills. Urban-suburban fabric with multi-family homes, pedestrian commercial streets, and vibrant Latino and Middle Eastern cultural commerce.
neighborhoods.taxDynamic: Highest tax-to-income burden (13.82%). Over 58% of households rent. Major contributor to elementary and middle school enrollment.

neighborhoods.name: Lakeview & Dutch Hill
neighborhoods.description: Northern Clifton bordering Paterson. Features a diverse mix of 2-family homes, bungalows, and multi-family properties with high family density.
neighborhoods.taxDynamic: Younger population with high child-to-adult ratio. Generates significant public school enrollment while facing high effective tax burdens relative to household earnings.

keyTakeaways.title: The 56.7% Income Gap Between ZIP Codes
keyTakeaways.detail: Median household income in 07013 ($116,273) is $42,079 higher than in 07011 ($74,194). This creates a stark division in economic resilience to property tax increases.

keyTakeaways.title: The Inverted Tax Burden (Tax Effort vs. Ability to Pay)
keyTakeaways.detail: Although 07013 pays higher nominal tax bills ($14.2k vs $10.0k), residents in 07011 pay a higher portion of their paycheck on property taxes (13.55% of household income vs. 12.24% in 07013).

keyTakeaways.title: The Inter-Neighborhood School Subsidy
keyTakeaways.detail: 07013 generates ~63% of Clifton's residential tax levy while supplying ~47% of students. 07011 supplies ~53% of public school students while contributing ~37% of the residential tax levy.

keyTakeaways.title: The Hidden Renter Burden
keyTakeaways.detail: 52% of 07011 households are renters. Because multi-family landlords pass 100% of property taxes into leases, working-class tenants pay an estimated $300 to $450 of their monthly rent directly toward municipal and school taxes.
